title: Shoulder dystocia
summary: Failure of the shoulders to deliver spontaneously after the head, requiring additional obstetric manoeuvres.

blocks.heading: Actions — HELPERR
bullets: Call for help immediately — senior midwife, obstetrician, neonatal team; note the time.
H — Call for Help, note the time.
E — Evaluate for Episiotomy (to allow room for manoeuvres, not to relieve bony obstruction itself).
L — Legs: McRoberts manoeuvre (hyperflex maternal hips onto abdomen).
P — suprapubic Pressure applied by an assistant.
E — Enter manoeuvres: internal rotational manoeuvres (e.g. Rubin II / Wood's screw).
R — Roll the woman onto all fours (if not already attempted) and repeat manoeuvres.
Avoid fundal pressure and excessive traction throughout — associated with increased injury.
Note the time of head delivery and time of body delivery, and which manoeuvres were used, for the record and neonatal handover.

blocks.heading: What to document
bullets: Time of head delivery and time of body delivery (head-to-body interval).
Manoeuvres used, in order, and by whom.
Neonatal condition at birth and any signs of injury (e.g. brachial plexus, fracture).
Maternal injury assessment (perineal/anal sphincter, PPH risk).
